title: Connect a data source and query it

blocks.content: A system you already run holds your data. You'll connect Grafana Cloud to it, test the connection, and run a first query. The data stays where it is.
First, add the connection. You need the **Admin** role in your stack:
Search for the system that holds your data, for example InfluxDB or CloudWatch, then select it from the results.
blocks.tooltip: Type the name of the system you already run. The results filter as you type.

blocks.content: On your data source's page, click **Add new data source**.
Grafana names the data source for you. To rename it, click the pencil icon next to the default name and enter something you'll recognize later.
Fill in the connection details. The fields depend on your system, but every data source asks two things: where the data lives, and how to sign in.
Click **Save & test**. It saves the connection and checks that it works.
Your data source is connected and tested.
Now confirm you can query it:
Open the data source picker and choose the data source you just added.
blocks.tooltip: Every query runs against one of your connected data stores. This picker chooses which one.

blocks.content: > **Note:** The query editor below the picker is specific to your data source and uses its own query language. For example, data that lives in InfluxDB is queried in InfluxQL.
In the query editor, write a small query. Ask for one thing you know your system holds.
Click **Run query**. Your results appear below the query editor.

You queried your own data in place. Nothing was copied into Grafana Cloud, so this connection doesn't add to the usage Grafana Cloud bills for. When a query is worth keeping, build a dashboard from it.
